clues: This city sits at the south west tip of the North Island, by Cook Strait. Hills of the Remutaka Range rise just behind it.
This is the windiest city on Earth, by mean wind speed. Cold south blasts in winter can make the air feel far colder than it is.
The capital moved to this city in 1865, taking the job from Auckland. Law makers had first met here three years before that.
A cable car climbs from the main shopping street to a hill suburb high over the harbour. The ride takes just five minutes, end to end.
The parliament of New Zealand meets in this city, and its top court sits here too. Most state services are based in its streets.
